commands.name: read_radar_tracks
commands.who: ComputerCraft program on a computer wired to the dish
commands.what: load the current Create Radar track list from a dish that is not on the gun bearing
commands.when: a Create Radar dish is attached; each time a caller needs this tick's tracks
commands.where: Amazeballs world, ComputerCraft peripheral wrap on that computer
commands.why: Create Radar yaw and pitch controllers drive cannon mounts, not Simulated swivel bearings, so this program must read tracks itself
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.read_radar_tracks(opts); opts omitted, nil, or a table whose keys are a subset of inputs

inputs.radar_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; rotating dish or plane radar peripheral name; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover
inputs.monitor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; Create Radar monitor peripheral name; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover; name only a monitor by setting this key and omitting radar_name

commands.name: read_swivel_bearing_angle
commands.who: ComputerCraft program wired to a Simulated swivel bearing
commands.what: read the stored servo target in degrees via getTargetAngle; visual or physics orientation is out of reach
commands.where: Amazeballs world, native swivel ComputerCraft wrap
commands.why: closed-loop rotate needs the angle; native wrap is read-only
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.read_swivel_bearing_angle(opts); opts omitted, nil, or a table whose keys are a subset of inputs; success is one Lua number in degrees

inputs.bearing_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; swivel_bearing peripheral name; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover

outputs.angle_degrees: one Lua number; stored servo target; bearing-local degrees about FACING; remainder negatives from Java %= 360 are allowed; the number already includes Simulated's FACING-negative kinetic speed flip; callers must not re-apply that flip; after disassemble and before the next writer, the number is 0; still one Lua number

commands.name: set_electric_motor_speed
commands.who: ComputerCraft program wired to a Create Crafts and Additions electric motor
commands.what: set that motor's commanded speed; skip setSpeed when getSpeed already equals rpm; getSpeed is commanded motorSpeed; an out-of-range rpm never equals getSpeed after Java clamp so those calls always write; unpowered or redstone-POWERED motors still succeed and still skip
commands.where: Amazeballs world, kinetic network on the bearing
commands.why: bearings turn from kinetic input; this is the write primitive; native swivel wrap cannot set angle
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.set_electric_motor_speed(opts); opts is a table; success is no return values

inputs.motor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; electric_motor peripheral name; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover
inputs.rpm: required finite Lua number; passed to setSpeed as a number; Java clamps to configured RPM range

commands.name: fire_rotating_barrel
commands.who: ComputerCraft program on the gun computer
commands.what: pulse analog strength 1 for two game ticks on the Create Big Cannons mount fire face, then 0, so the rotating autocannon fires once
commands.when: the barrel loop is spinning and a shot is wanted
commands.where: Amazeballs world. Mount fire face, separate from the aim motors. ComputerCraft redstone API or a redstone_relay on that face
commands.why: Create Big Cannons has no ComputerCraft fire method; the native trigger is analog redstone on the mount fire face. Aim does not pull the trigger
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.fire_rotating_barrel(opts); opts is a table; success is no return values

inputs.side: required string on the Lua opts table; ComputerCraft side name: top, bottom, left, right, front, or back
inputs.relay_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; redstone_relay peripheral name; omit key, nil, or empty string to use the computer redstone API

commands.name: rotate_bearing_toward_angle
commands.who: ComputerCraft program on the gun computer
commands.what: one closed-loop step: read one stored swivel target, command one motor toward a commanded angle, return signed shortest-path error; does not sleep until arrival and does not wait for Simulated integration or cc_update_rpm; every success that reaches set_electric_motor_speed inherits that child's getSpeed main-thread yield, and setSpeed when that child writes
commands.when: the bearing and motor peripherals are attached and a target angle is known
commands.where: Amazeballs world, one electric motor on one Simulated swivel bearing (intended world, not a runtime kinetic-connectivity test); bearing_name and motor_name identify which child wrap to read and which child wrap to write; they do not assert that the named motor drives the named bearing; omit, nil, or empty-string discovery still does not prove shaft membership
commands.why: native swivel wrap cannot set angle; kinetic input is the write path; aim composes this once per axis
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.rotate_bearing_toward_angle(opts); opts is a table; success is one Lua number, signed shortest-path error in degrees; leftover inside the tolerance band is still that number, including when the motor is commanded 0; magnitude is at most 180; success that reaches the motor write is not yield-free: getSpeed always yields on that child, setSpeed yields when that child writes; read_swivel_bearing_angle may yield if its getter is main-thread

inputs.target_degrees: required finite Lua number; commanded stored servo target in degrees; compared on the remainder circle to read_swivel_bearing_angle
inputs.rpm: required finite Lua number; motor command whose sign increases the stored field; the write is 0 if and only if abs(shortest-path error) is less than or equal to the resolved tolerance; otherwise that value when the error is positive, and its negation when the error is negative; 0 is a legal stop-only step
inputs.bearing_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; passed through to read_swivel_bearing_angle; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover
inputs.motor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; passed through to set_electric_motor_speed; omit key, nil, or empty string to discover
inputs.tolerance_degrees: optional finite Lua number greater than or equal to 0; omit key or nil means 1; empty string is not default and fails as a non-number; motor is commanded 0 when abs(error) is less than or equal to this

outputs.error_degrees: one Lua number; signed shortest-path error in degrees from the stored servo target to target_degrees; positive means the stored field must increase; Java remainder negatives from the child read are allowed and wrapped here; 180 chooses the positive path; magnitude is at most 180; leftover inside the tolerance band is still returned, including when the motor is commanded 0; success is not 0 merely because the motor stopped

commands.name: aim_turret_at_target
commands.who: ComputerCraft program on the gun computer
commands.what: confirm a live radar target this tick and drive yaw and pitch Simulated swivel bearings to caller-supplied ballistic degrees
commands.when: a firing solution exists and a Create Radar dish is attached
commands.where: Amazeballs world; kinetic motors on Simulated yaw and pitch swivel bearings
commands.why: Create Radar yaw and pitch controllers drive cannon mounts, not this Lua path; this command aims bearings at a solution and does not compute Going Ballistic physics
commands.call: Lua bearing_turret.aim_turret_at_target(opts); opts is a table; success is no return values

inputs.yaw_degrees: required finite Lua number; bearing-local degrees for the yaw swivel; from the caller (compute_ballistic_aim)
inputs.pitch_degrees: required finite Lua number; bearing-local degrees for the pitch swivel; from the caller (compute_ballistic_aim)
inputs.track_id: optional string on the Lua opts table; live radar track id to require this tick; omit key, nil, or empty string to use the monitor selectedTrackId from read_radar_tracks
inputs.radar_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to read_radar_tracks
inputs.monitor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to read_radar_tracks
inputs.yaw_bearing_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to rotate_bearing_toward_angle for the yaw axis
inputs.pitch_bearing_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to rotate_bearing_toward_angle for the pitch axis
inputs.yaw_motor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to rotate_bearing_toward_angle for the yaw axis
inputs.pitch_motor_name: optional string on the Lua opts table; forwarded to rotate_bearing_toward_angle for the pitch axis
